title: KV cache hierarchical quantization probe with sentinel quality monitors
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Measure quality vs. memory trade-offs for a hierarchical, context-sensitive KV cache quantization strategy and validate production-safe sentinel monitors that trigger per-request fallbacks. This ticket covers: design of a multi-tier quant storage (hot FP8 / warm INT8 / cold INT4), fuzzy prefix-aware quant scheduling, experiment harness for throughput/latency/quality, and integration of sentinel monitors to avoid user-visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment harness runs on target hardware and produces reproducible metrics for at least three models (13B instruction, 33B chat, 70B decoder)
A candidate hierarchical quant profile reduces KV memory footprint by >=35% vs baseline FP16 with <3% relative degradation on token-level cross-entropy for the instruction suite
Sentinel monitors detect >90% of generated samples with quality regressions above defined thresholds and trigger automatic per-request fallback to higher-fidelity storage
Implementation has a clear rollback path (transparent per-request override) and an infra cost estimate for Dedicated customers
Experiment artifacts (scripts, datasets, result dashboards) are linked in the ticket and reproducible within CI
experiment_plan:
Overview: run controlled comparisons between baseline (FP16 KV), flat quant schemes (FP8-only, INT8-only, INT4-only), and a hierarchical scheme that stores recent tokens in FP8, mid-age tokens in INT8, and long-tail tokens in INT4. Introduce two dynamic policies: (1) cohort-aware fidelity — adapt per-request bitwidth based on client cohort (interactive vs batch), and (2) prefix-weighted allocation — keep the last N tokens in higher fidelity depending on model context-length distribution. For each configuration we will sweep kernel/path choices (cuBLAS/explicit kernels), batching parameters (continuous batching target batch sizes 1..32), and KV sharding strategies. Each trial collects: token-level cross-entropy, MRR on retrieval-style evals, end-to-end 95th latency, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), GPU memory high-water mark, and SLO violation rate. Run matrix across A100-40GB and H100-80GB in dedicated cluster with identical model weights. Implementation steps:
- Week 1: implement hierarchical storage prototype in runtime (storage layer + bitpackers + fallback hooks) and add instrumentation hooks for sentinel signals.
- Week 2: add evaluation harness and dataset loaders, implement policy toggles (cohort/prefix), and prepare job orchestration.
- Week 3: run sweep, aggregate results to dashboard, and analyze failure cases to refine sentinel thresholds.
- Week 4: write PR to runtime with runtime flags and QA checklist for staged rollout
evaluation_metrics: fallback_rate (percentage of requests falling back to higher fidelity)
implementation_notes: Design decisions: 1) Use hybrid storage format with tag bytes per KV block to allow O(1) fallback to FP8/FP16 storage for hot ranges. 2) Prioritize last-k tokens for higher fidelity via a sliding window; warm tokens demote asynchronously to lower-bit storage to avoid latency spikes. 3) Implement sentinel monitors based on combined signals: token-level logprob shifts, ngram novelty delta, and end-task metric proxies (e.g., paraphrase similarity). 4) Keep runtime fallback as an inline fast-path to read higher-fidelity KV when sentinel threshold exceeded. Engineering trade-offs: extra metadata bytes reduce theoretical memory wins but are necessary for reliable fallbacks; asynchronous demotion reduces tail latency risk but increases code complexity. Edge cases: extremely long single-turn generations where demotion may thrash — include hysteresis on demotion frequency.
rollout_and_fallback: Canary: sample 5% of traffic (non-paying sandbox) with sentinel-only monitoring (no fallback) for 48h
Stage: enable per-request fallback for canary cohort for additional 72h and monitor fallback_rate and error budgets
Full rollout: gate by fallback_rate < 2% and median latency within SLO
Rollback: runtime flag to force baseline FP16 KV for any customer or model version
